explanations: The Sun is the star at the centre of the Solar System, a sphere of hot plasma holding 99.86 per cent of the system's mass.
The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, about 384,400 kilometres away and tidally locked so that one side always faces us.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun, the only place known to harbour life, with an ocean over 70.8 per cent of its crust.
A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, hiding the Sun from a small part of the world.

sources.excerpt: The Sun is the star located at the centre of the Solar System. It is a massive sphere of hot plasma, heated to incandescence by nuclear fusion reactions in its core, radiating the energy from its surface mainly as visible light and infrared radiation with 10% at ultraviolet energies.
The Sun's mass is around 330,000 times that of Earth, making up about 99.86% of the total mass of the Solar System.
The Moon is the only natural satellite of Earth. It orbits Earth at an average distance of 384,399 kilometers (238,854 mi).
The resulting tidal forces are the main driver of Earth's tides, and have pulled the Moon to always face Earth with the same near side.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only astronomical object known to harbor life.
Almost all of Earth's water is contained in its ocean, which covers 70.8% of Earth's crust.
A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, thereby obscuring the view of the Sun from a small part of Earth, totally or partially.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: a lunar eclipse also lines up the same three bodies, but with Earth in the middle, and can be seen from anywhere on the night side, which the final hint rules out; 'the Solar System' holds all three but is not an event; a new moon happens monthly without an eclipse.
